done_when: The shared test lane admits one test run per four available cores, at least one (two on an 8-core machine), each test command still getting half the machine's cores as its worker count; forge doctor, the lanes view and the pane show the test lane's size; the coordinator guide says so; command tests cover an 8-core machine admitting two test runs while a third waits, and a 4-core machine keeping one, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: This function and tests/test_machine_test_lane_capacity_pane.py:62 lack criterion numbers. tests/test_rules.py:45–50 requires every test function, including fixes, to match `test_<number>_<rule>` and requires distinct numbers within the shared STORY. Consequently, the full-suite CI command at .github/workflows/forge-next.yml:80 will fail. The supplied 42-test close run omitted test_rules.py, so its green result does not catch this. Number both functions distinctly and update their proof-list references.
findings.title: Number both new tests to keep the full suite passing

findings.body: The previously reported clipping remains. At 60 columns, two running tests produce a 37-column counts string; an active Tests stage and total time of 100 seconds add 28 columns. pane.ts:137–143 reserves both with flexShrink: 0, allocating 65 columns even after title and tail widths reach zero. This clips timing in compact terminal and desktop prompts. Budget counts and timing together. The command-backed 60-column test concatenates text without checking allocated widths; native compact checks cover 79 columns.
findings.title: Keep expanded compact counts within the prompt width

why: The machine-wide test lane runs one test run at a time, so on an 8-core machine three or more closes and worker test runs often queue behind each other while cores sit idle (owner, 2026-10-09: two test runs at once, each with half the cores)
